page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor featuring 12 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel processing workloads are accelerated by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 48 GB of dedicated VRAM.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range, reflecting the shared CPU allocation model. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is strong, ranking in the top 25% for both read and write operations. The hardware excels in LLM inference tasks, achieving top-tier text generation speeds of 368.94 tokens per second with a small 135M model and strong performance of 36.32 tokens per second with a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a high-capacity GPU and substantial memory allocation relative to its 12 vCPUs. However, users must note that local storage is not bundled with this instance, meaning external storage solutions must be attached. The shared CPU allocation also introduces potential performance variability under sustained multi-core CPU loads, though the underlying AMD EPYC 9575F hardware mitigates this with strong single-threaded execution.

This server configuration is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, small to medium large language model execution, and image processing. It is also appropriate for single-threaded data decompression tasks and memory-intensive applications that do not require dedicated, non-shared multi-core CPU resources.
